title: The world remembers Jesus as the Lamb who was crucified.
paragraphs:
The world remembers Jesus as the Lamb who was crucified.
But the Bible also reveals the day He will return as the King who conquers.

Many people picture Jesus as gentle, quiet, and harmless — a teacher who spoke about love and forgiveness. And that is true. He came the first time in humility, wearing a crown of thorns, rejected by the world He came to save.
But Scripture makes something clear that many people overlook.
The same Jesus who was mocked, beaten, and crucified will one day return in glory, power, and authority.
In Revelation 19:11–16, heaven opens and a breathtaking scene unfolds.

Christ appears riding a white horse.
His eyes blaze like fire.
He wears many crowns.
His robe is dipped in blood.
And the armies of heaven follow Him.
The Bible gives Him a title written on His robe and thigh:
KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS.

This is the moment when history reaches its turning point.
Every earthly power that thought it ruled the world will fall.
Every hidden injustice will be exposed.
Every lie will collapse before the truth of the returning King.
For some, this day will be the greatest joy imaginable — the long-awaited return of the Savior.
For others, it will be the most terrifying realization in history.
Because the question is not whether Jesus will return.
The question is whether we are ready to meet Him.

Right now, the door of grace is still open.
Right now, mercy is still available.
Right now, anyone who calls on His name can receive forgiveness and new life.
But the Bible reminds us that history is moving toward a moment when the King will return.
And when that day comes…
every eye will see Him.
Take a moment to reflect on this.

If Christ returned tonight…
Would you be ready to stand before Him?
The King is coming. 👑📖
